title: Write-up calls the probability gap 'the edge', which is a different number from the edge % shown on the same pick
steps: Saint Mary's Gaels ML pick: writeup.edge = 'The price ... (−196) implies 66%; we make it 71%. That 4.9-point gap is the edge.' The same pick shows edge +7.3% (0.7109×1.51−1 = 0.0735).
UNLV Rebels ML: '…implies 68%; we make it 69%. That 1.5-point gap is the edge.' Displayed edge +2.2% (0.6904×1.48−1 = 0.0218).
expected: One meaning of 'edge' on the page: either say 'a 4.9-point probability gap, worth +7.3% expected value', or don't call the gap the edge.
actual: The text calls 4.9 points 'the edge' next to a +7.3% edge badge; a bettor checking the math sees two different edges. (The underlying numbers are right: implied 1/1.51 = 66.2%, fair 71.1%, gap 4.86 pts.)
persona: sharp bettor who checks the math
